2.5.3.1-r1.burton_quote: which works better and speedier than any simple whatsoever, and much to be preferred before all those fulsome decoctions, and infusions, which must offend by reason of their quantity; this alone in a small measure taken, expels wind, and that most forcibly, moves urine, cleanseth the stomach of all gross humours, crudities, helps appetite, &c.

2.5.3.1-r10.burton_quote: In crudity (saith Piso) ’tis good to bind the stomach hard

2.5.3.1-r11.burton_quote: Dropaces of pitch, and oil of Rue, applied at certain times to the stomach, to the metaphrenum

2.5.3.1-r12.burton_quote: would have the thighs to be cauterized

2.5.3.1-r2.burton_quote: and these must be often used, still abstaining from those which are more violent, lest they do exasperate the stomach

2.5.3.1-r3.burton_quote: forbids cold medicines, because they increase obstructions, and other bad symptoms

2.5.3.1-r4.burton_quote: The stomach most part in this infirmity is cold, the liver hot; scarce therefore (which Montanus insinuates consil. 229 for the Earl of Montfort) can you help the one, and not hurt the other

2.5.3.1-r5.burton_quote: but it was after signified to him in letters, that the decoction of China and Sassafras, and salt of Sassafras, wrought him an incredible good

2.5.3.1-r6.burton_quote: cured an exceeding great swelling of the spleen with Capers alone, a meat befitting that infirmity, and frequent use of the water of a Smith’s forge
2.5.3.1-r6.translation: the swelling was incurable; the water was water in which a blacksmith had often quenched red-hot iron

2.5.3.1-r7.burton_quote: that those creatures as drink of it, have commonly little or no spleen

2.5.3.1-r8.burton_quote: to other men (saith he) this opening of the haemorrhoids seems to be a profitable remedy; for my part I do not approve of it, because it draws away the thinnest blood, and leaves the thickest behind

2.5.3.1-r9.burton_quote: I have found (saith he) by experience, that many hypochondriacal melancholy men have been cured by the sole use of Clysters
